payload.roles:
- The owner: rules the design, holds the push, and is the one harmed when a ship silently produces nothing.
- The driving agent: runs the iteration, and needs its work durable from the first milestone rather than only at the close.
- The future reader of the ledger: opens trunk expecting live claims, and pays for every event that leaks onto it.
- The auditor of a past decision: asks how a shipped iteration reached its ruling, and needs the record to still exist and be findable.
- The board and the projections: read what the close leaves behind; they are affected here even though they are not changed here.
- The maintainer of the git repository (the owner, in another hat): carries the cost of history that can never be rewritten.
payload.tensions:
T1 - the future reader versus the auditor. The reader wants trunk to hold only what is true now; the auditor wants everything the decision rested on to remain. RESOLUTION: the two-parent filtered merge serves both - claims on trunk, events under the tag - and where they still collide, nothing-lost wins, so a close that cannot guarantee reachability refuses.

T2 - the driving agent versus the future reader. Frequent milestone commits are what make the agent's work durable, and every one of them is noise the reader must never see. RESOLUTION: the branch absorbs the frequency; trunk changes exactly once per iteration, at the close.

T3 - the auditor versus the git maintainer. A complete record means history that can never be rewritten, which means the repository only grows. RESOLUTION: accepted, and already the design's stance - SE refuses rebase and force-push on published branches; the mitigation is partial clone when size ever bites, not deletion.

T4 - the owner versus the driving agent. The owner wants a ship to be trustworthy without watching it; the agent, running unattended, is exactly who benefits from a close that reports success. RESOLUTION: the empty-branch guard - the agent may not be told merged when nothing merged; this is why that guard is a requirement and not a nicety.
